What is Trusted Advisor and in which categories does it give recommendations?

Trusted Advisor is a high-level assessment service for your AWS account, with nothing to install. It gives recommendations in six categories: cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, service limits and operational excellence. With a Business or Enterprise plan, you get all the checks and programmatic access via the AWS Support API. For example, it flags an open port in a security group or the absence of MFA on the root.
How can a cost anomaly reveal a compromise?

An attacker who steals an IAM key often launches many EC2 instances to mine cryptocurrency, sometimes in an unused Region. Cost Anomaly Detection learns the spending history by ML, without a threshold, and alerts with a root cause analysis (service, account, Region, usage type). You then investigate with CloudTrail, disable the compromised key, terminate the instances and add an SCP that forbids unused Regions.
What is the difference between Cost Explorer, Cost Anomaly Detection and Budgets?

Cost Explorer is used to analyze and visualize costs, make forecasts and choose a Savings Plan. Cost Anomaly Detection automatically detects unusual spikes by ML without a threshold and gives the root cause. AWS Budgets alerts when a threshold set in advance is reached. The three complement each other.
What is the AWS Acceptable Use Policy for?

The AUP defines the prohibited uses of AWS services: illegal or fraudulent activities, infringement of others' rights, threats and violence, child abuse content, harm to the security of other networks and spam. AWS may remove or disable the offending content. If my compromised resources attack third parties, I may receive an abuse report and I must react.
